steps.title: Understand the reduce method and its purpose
steps.instruction: Read about how the reduce method works on arrays to accumulate values into a single result.
steps.hint: Think about how you might sum an array of numbers or combine multiple strings into one.
steps.seedCode: // No code yet — this is a reading step about reduce.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll understand that reduce transforms an array into a single value by applying a function to each element.
successCriteria: You can explain in your own words what the reduce method does and why it's useful.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've grasped the purpose of reduce: it accumulates array elements into one result.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Remember, reduce processes each element to build up a final value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's review: reduce takes an array and combines all its elements into a single output using a callback.

steps.title: Create the function signature for customReduce
steps.instruction: Create a function named customReduce that accepts three parameters: an array, a callback function, and an initial value.
steps.hint: Think about the basic structure of a function declaration or arrow function with three parameters.
steps.seedCode:
// No code yet — this is a reading step about reduce.

// Create your customReduce function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named customReduce is defined with three parameters.
successCriteria: The code contains a function named customReduce that accepts three parameters (array, callback, and initialValue).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the function signature for customReduce with the correct parameters.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named exactly 'customReduce' and accepts all three parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function signature isn't quite right. Create a function named customReduce that takes an array, a callback function, and an initial value as parameters.

steps.title: Initialize the accumulator variable
steps.instruction: Inside your customReduce function, check if an initial value is provided. If it is, set the accumulator variable to that initial value. If not, set the accumulator to the first element of the array.
steps.hint: Use an if statement to check if the initialValue argument is undefined. If it is, set accumulator to array[0]; otherwise, set accumulator to initialValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The accumulator variable is properly initialized based on whether initialValue is provided.
successCriteria: The accumulator variable is declared and set to either initialValue or the first array element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly initialized the accumulator variable based on the presence of initialValue.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your initialization logic. Make sure accumulator is set to initialValue when provided, otherwise to the first array element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The accumulator initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to check if initialValue is provided and set accumulator accordingly.

steps.title: Set up the starting index for iteration
steps.instruction: Inside the customReduce function, declare a variable named 'startIndex' and set it to 0 if initialValue is provided, otherwise set it to 1.
steps.hint: You can use a conditional (if/else) or a ternary operator to check if initialValue is not undefined.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have a 'startIndex' variable that correctly determines where to begin iterating through the array.
successCriteria: A variable named 'startIndex' is declared and assigned the value 0 when initialValue is provided, or 1 when it's not.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly set up the starting index based on whether an initial value is provided.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your logic. The starting index should be 0 when initialValue is given, otherwise 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The starting index isn't set correctly. Remember: if initialValue is provided, start at index 0; if not, start at index 1 (using the first array element as the initial value).

steps.title: Create the loop to iterate through array elements
steps.instruction: Inside your customReduce function, add a for loop that iterates through the array starting from the index you determined earlier.
steps.hint: Use a standard for loop with the starting index variable you created in the previous step.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your customReduce function will have a for loop that can iterate through the array elements.
successCriteria: A for loop is added inside the customReduce function that uses the starting index variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the iteration loop. This will allow your reduce implementation to process each array element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your for loop starts from the correct index variable and iterates through all array elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The for loop structure doesn't match what's needed. Remember to create a standard for loop that starts from the index variable and goes through all array elements.

steps.title: Apply the callback function to each element
steps.instruction: Inside your for loop, call the callback function with the accumulator, current element, index, and array, then update the accumulator with the returned value.
steps.hint: The callback should be called with four arguments: accumulator, array[i], i, and array. Assign the result back to accumulator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The loop now properly calls the callback function on each iteration, updating the accumulator with the result.
successCriteria: The callback function is called inside the loop with accumulator, current element, index, and array, and the accumulator is updated with the returned value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly implemented the callback application inside the loop. This is the core logic that makes reduce work.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling the callback with all four arguments (accumulator, current element, index, array) and updating the accumulator with the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The callback function needs to be called inside the loop with the proper arguments and the accumulator needs to be updated with the returned value.

steps.title: Return the final accumulated value
steps.instruction: After the for loop in your customReduce function, return the accumulator variable.
steps.hint: Add a return statement at the end of your function to output the final accumulated result.
steps.expectedOutcome: The customReduce function will now return the final accumulated value after processing all array elements.
successCriteria: The function ends with a return statement that returns the accumulator variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've completed the core logic of customReduce by returning the final accumulated value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning the accumulator variable at the end of the function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't return the accumulator. Add a return statement after the loop.

steps.title: Test the customReduce function with a simple example
steps.instruction: Create a test array of numbers and use your customReduce function to sum them, then log the result to the console.
steps.hint: Define an array like [1, 2, 3, 4], then call customReduce with a callback that adds each element to the accumulator. Start with an initial value of 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: The console should display the sum of the test array numbers (e.g., 10 for [1,2,3,4]).
successCriteria: A test array is defined, customReduce is called with a sum callback and initial value, and the result is logged to console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully tested your customReduce function with a basic sum operation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you defined an array, called customReduce with the correct arguments, and logged the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test isn't working yet. Check that you defined an array, used customReduce with a sum callback, and logged the output.

steps.title: Test with different initial values
steps.instruction: Add a test case to verify that your customReduce function works correctly when called without an initial value.
steps.hint: Call customReduce with only two arguments: the array and the callback. The function should use the first array element as the initial accumulator value.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your test will demonstrate that customReduce can handle cases where no initialValue is provided, using the first array element as the starting accumulator.
successCriteria: A test case is added that calls customReduce with only array and callback arguments (no initialValue).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a test case without an initial value. This will help verify your function handles optional arguments correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your test calls customReduce with only two arguments (array and callback) to test the no-initial-value case.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on testing without an initial value. Add a call to customReduce that passes only the array and callback function.

steps.title: Test with complex callback functions
steps.instruction: Add a test case that uses your customReduce function with a callback that finds the maximum value in an array of numbers.
steps.hint: Create a test array of numbers and use a callback that compares the accumulator with the current element to keep the larger value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should see that your customReduce function correctly identifies the maximum value when tested with an array of numbers.
successCriteria: A test case is added that uses customReduce with a callback function to find the maximum value in an array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your customReduce function successfully handles complex callback logic like finding maximum values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a test case, but make sure it uses a proper callback function that compares values to find the maximum.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test case is missing or doesn't properly test finding the maximum value with customReduce.
